claims.text: The baseline alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi in a solid-solution state.
The modified material is a Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy prepared using the same processing history as the baseline.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi increases the alloy's stacking-fault energy.
The increase in stacking-fault energy caused by Co removal suppresses deformation twinning.
Stacking-fault energy controls the relative activation of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
Twin-boundary density and dislocation arrangement can indicate the relative activity of twinning and dislocation slip.
At low temperatures and/or high strain rates, deformation twinning contributes to strain hardening and ductility in Co-containing CoCrFeMnNi.
Under low-temperature and/or high-strain-rate conditions, the Co-free alloy deforms mainly by dislocation slip rather than twinning.
At higher temperatures, activated cross-slip and dynamic recovery may partially compensate for reduced twinning.
Cross-slip and dynamic recovery at higher temperatures affect yield strength and ductility.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, the Co-free alloy will exhibit less deformation twinning.
Reduced twinning in the Co-free alloy will produce lower strain hardening at low temperature and high strain rate.
The Co-free alloy may have higher yield strength than CoCrFeMnNi at low temperature and high strain rate.
Differences between the alloys will be less pronounced at higher temperatures and low strain rates because of enhanced dynamic recovery.
CoCrFeMnNi exhibits an active contribution from deformation twinning to its strength–ductility balance under comparable testing conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies to solidified, single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloys from approximately -196 °C to room temperature and strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1.
A controlled comparison should use identical casting, homogenization, and solid-solution heat-treatment protocols for the Co-containing and Co-free alloys.
Interrupted mechanical tests followed by TEM can quantify deformation-twin density and characterize dislocation structures.

The hypothesis is falsified if the Co-free alloy shows no statistically significant reduction in twinning density or corresponding strain-hardening changes relative to CoCrFeMnNi across the tested regimes.
